investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 6-node cluster reported 2 nodes with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes that did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, with preemption unable to help. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota for peer-pod VMs was exhausted or the allocatable count was zero), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod stayed unschedulable for 134–143 seconds, the eval runner timed out before the agent reached a ready state, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 6-node cluster reported 2 nodes with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes that did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, with preemption unable to help. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota for peer-pod VMs was exhausted or the allocatable count was zero), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod stayed unschedulable for 134–143 seconds, the eval runner timed out before the agent reached a ready state, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — all allocatable peer-pod VM slots are in use by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests.

[Likely] The 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at all (wrong node pool, missing device plugin, or missing node label), so only 2 nodes are ever eligible and both are saturated.

[Possible] A peer-pod device plugin or node agent on the 2 eligible nodes is unhealthy or has not re-advertised capacity after a restart, causing the allocatable count to read as 0 even if physical capacity exists.

[Possible] The pod's node affinity or node selector was recently tightened (e.g., a label change on the node pool) so that fewer nodes qualify, reducing the scheduling surface to only the 2 already-saturated nodes.

[Lower likelihood] A prior eval run or leaked remote agent pod is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that were not released by the cleanup path in withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs), progressively exhausting capacity across runs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-15 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes VM-capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent for a "remote" agent (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the resulting pod was left Unschedulable for ~143 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, no agent was created, no runtime response was obtained, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. The same scheduling error message appears across all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create at ~134 s, remote-agent-state at ~143 s, remote-agent-runtime at ~143 s), confirming the failure is rooted in cluster-level VM resource exhaustion rather than in application logic or eval configuration.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent eval runs, other workloads, or leaked/stuck pods from prior runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is always just 2 nodes; any saturation of those 2 nodes causes total unavailability.

Tertiary — pod preemption disabled or ineffective: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' indicates no lower-priority pods exist on the eligible nodes that could be evicted to free capacity.

Quaternary — resource leak from a prior eval run: if a previous remote-agent pod was not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 may not have run if the runner was interrupted), it could be holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and blocking new scheduling.
